Buying SIM Cards at Jeddah Airport: STC vs Mobily vs Zain

STC, Mobily or Zain? How to buy a visitor SIM at Jeddah Airport (JED), what documents you need, eSIM alternatives, and staying reachable on the way to Makkah.

By Taxi Saudi Arabia Editorial TeamPublished 27 September 2026Updated 2 October 20263 min read

Quick answer

STC, Mobily and Zain all sell visitor SIM cards in the arrivals area at King Abdulaziz International Airport (JED). You need your passport and a fingerprint scan, which the kiosk staff do on the spot. If the kiosk queue is long, you can buy a SIM later in Makkah, Madinah or Jeddah city — just make sure your transfer is pre-booked so you are not relying on mobile data to find a ride.

  2. The three operators compared

Why sort out connectivity before you leave the airport

Most things you will do in your first hour in Saudi Arabia — messaging your driver, opening your hotel booking, using maps, paying by phone — assume you have mobile data. At King Abdulaziz International Airport (JED) the three Saudi operators, STC, Mobily and Zain, all sell visitor SIM cards and data packages in the arrivals area, so you can be connected before you walk out to the kerb.

The three operators compared

Packages and prices change often, so compare what is on the kiosk board on the day rather than relying on any article. The differences that tend to matter for visitors:

STCMobilyZain
Who it isThe largest and longest-established operatorThe second-largest operatorThe third national operator
Typical visitor offerShort-stay visitor bundles with data and some international minutesData-focused visitor bundles, often with social-app add-onsValue-focused data bundles
Worth considering if…You will travel between cities and want the widest networkYou stay mostly in the big cities and use a lot of dataPrice per GB matters most

Coverage in Jeddah, Makkah, Madinah and Riyadh is good on all three. On long desert highways coverage can drop for stretches on any network — something to keep in mind if you are travelling between cities and want to stay reachable.

What you need to buy a SIM

  • Your passport with your entry visa.
  • A fingerprint scan — registering a SIM to your identity with a fingerprint is mandatory in Saudi Arabia. The kiosk staff do it at the counter.
  • Payment by card or cash in Saudi riyals.

Activation is normally quick, but queues at the kiosks build up when several long-haul flights land together — common at night during the Umrah season.

eSIM and roaming alternatives

If your phone supports eSIM, a travel eSIM bought before you fly lets you land already connected and skip the kiosk entirely. Roaming on your home SIM also works but is usually the most expensive way to use data. Whichever you choose, check that your phone is unlocked if you plan to use a Saudi SIM.

If the queue is long

You do not have to buy a SIM at the airport. Operator shops are easy to find in Jeddah, in the hotel districts of Makkah and Madinah, and in Riyadh's malls. The one thing to avoid is arriving with no data and no pre-arranged way of leaving the airport:

  • Pre-book your transfer so you know who is collecting you and where.
  • Save the booking confirmation and the driver's WhatsApp number offline (a screenshot is enough).
  • Use the airport Wi-Fi to send a quick message on landing.

Connectivity on the road to Makkah and Madinah

The Jeddah Airport to Makkah transfer is about 80 km — roughly an hour — on a busy, well-covered expressway, so you will usually have signal the whole way. The Jeddah to Madinah drive is around four hours through open country, where coverage can be patchy in places; download offline maps and any documents you need before you set off.
